{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2024}}

'''Lionel Salem''' (5 March 1937 – 29 June 2024)<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eisenstein |first1=Odile |last2=Jean |first2=Yves |title=Disparition de Lionel Salem, grande figure de la chimie théorique |url=https://www.inc.cnrs.fr/fr/cnrsinfo/disparition-de-lionel-salem-grande-figure-de-la-chimie-theorique |website=cnrs CHIMIE |publisher=CNRS |access-date=22 November 2024 |language=FR |date=19 July 2024}}</ref> was a French [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]], former research director at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), retired since 1999.<ref>{{cite web|title=Organisation et moyens|url=http://www.cvc.u-psud.fr/ancien/Organisation.html|website=www.cvc.u-psud.fr|language=FR|access-date=15 October 2020}}</ref> He was a member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Past Members of the Academy|url=http://www.iaqms.org/past_members.php|website=IAQMS (International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science)|language=EN|access-date=25 January 2025|publication-date=}},</ref> which named him its annual award winner in 1975 ''for his work on photochemical processes and on chemical reaction mechanisms.''<ref>{{cite web|title=Award Winners|url=http://www.iaqms.org/awards.php|website=IAQMS (International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science|access-date=15 October 2020|archive-date=8 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908112331/http://www.iaqms.org/awards.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He has contributed to the theories of [[Intermolecular force|forces between molecules]], of [[Conjugated system|conjugated molecules]], of organic [[reaction mechanism]]s and of [[heterogeneous catalysis]]. He developed the electronic theory of [[Radical (chemistry)|diradicals]], as well as the concepts of [[diradical]] and [[zwitterion]]ic states.<ref name=IAQMS>{{Cite web |url=https://www.iaqms.org/members/salem.php|title=Lionel Salem|department=Members|website=[[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] (IAQMS)|location=[[Menton|Menton, France]]|language=en|access-date=2020-10-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240523144842/https://www.iaqms.org/members/salem.php|archive-date=2024-05-23|quote=Salem has made contributions to the theories of intermolecular forces, conjugated molecules, organic reaction mechanisms and heterogeneous catalysis}}</ref> In 1968, he described the energy change for the approach of two molecules as a function of their [[Molecular orbital|orbitals]]' properties; this approach, pursued independently by [[Gilles Klopman]], led to the [[Klopman–Salem equation]] and the theory of [[Frontier molecular orbital theory|frontier orbitals]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Salem|first1=Lionel|date=1 January 1968|title=Intermolecular orbital theory of the interaction between conjugated systems. I. General theory|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=90|issue=3|pages=543–552|doi=10.1021/ja01005a001}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Klopman|first1=Gilles|date=1 January 1968|title=Chemical reactivity and the concept of charge- and frontier-controlled reactions|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=90|issue=2|pages=223–234|doi=10.1021/ja01004a002}}</ref>

He is the author of several books on chemical subjects, including ''The Molecular Orbital Theory of Conjugated Systems'' (1966), ''The Organic Chemist's Book of Orbitals'' (with [[William L. Jorgensen]], 1973), ''The Marvelous Molecule'' (1979), and ''Electrons in Chemical Reactions'' (1982).<ref name="IAQMS" /><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Salem|first1=Lionel|title=Electrons in Chemical Reactions|publisher=Wiley-Interscience|year=1982|doi=10.1002/bbpc.19830870625|isbn=0-471-08474-3|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/bbpc.19830870625}}</ref> Salem died in Paris on 29 June 2024, at the age of 87.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 June 2024 |title=Lionel Samuel death notice |url=https://www.libramemoria.com/defunts/salem-lionel/065236a379d04cbbb9a48c0e6393289f |access-date=22 November 2024}}</ref>
